verdict.rationale: Obsidian's architecture structurally limits vendor access to user data. Notes are plain Markdown files stored locally under the user's "total control", and Sync uses default end-to-end encryption so that "not even the Obsidian team" can read notes. That implicitly prevents the vendor from training on note content. However, the evidence contains no explicit no-AI-training policy or opt-out control. Community plugins also run with full filesystem and network access, so third-party code could send vault data elsewhere. Missing for 10: an explicit first-party statement or policy that user data is not used for AI training, a user-facing training opt-out control, coverage of Publish-hosted content, and independent corroboration.
